title: When the Economy Changes Without the Economy Changing
subtitle: How national-accounts revisions propagate through narratives, ratios, economic structure and institutional classifications
abstract: A four-country forensic study of comprehensive national-accounts revisions. Rather than ranking revision magnitude, the release traces how documented measurement-system changes propagate into different downstream objects: Saudi Arabia's 2023 real-growth sign, Tunisia's GDP-denominated fiscal ratios, Morocco's measured sector composition and annual growth profile, and Jordan's World Bank income classification. The selected cases motivate a Measurement Shock Propagation Matrix and a larger pre-registered episode study.
headline_results: Saudi Arabia: 2023 real GDP growth -0.8% to +0.5% across pre- and post-comprehensive-revision vintages.
Tunisia: 2015 GDP level +6%; 2020 public debt/GDP 88.6% to 83.5% under the revised denominator.
Morocco: 2014 GDP level +8.2%; tertiary-sector share 51.6% to 54.8%; annual growth revisions move both up and down.
Jordan: World Bank states the comprehensive revision found the economy nearly 10% larger and, together with 2025 growth, pushed the country from lower-middle to upper-middle income.
review_status: Primary-source evidence assembled and arithmetic reproducible; selected forensic cases are not a representative regional sample; independent reproduction and larger pre-registered episode expansion pending.
claim_boundaries: No regional average revision is estimated.
Large revisions are not interpreted as manipulation, incompetence or statistical failure.
Comprehensive methodology shocks are separated from routine revisions.
GDP-denominated ratio changes are not equivalent to changes in nominal numerators.
Jordan's income reclassification is not attributed entirely to rebasing.
license: Lab-authored release; underlying official statistics remain subject to source terms.
